title: English: Grammar and Punctuation (B1-B2)
source: Written for Kru, Nov 24 (Henry): 100 questions on grammar, punctuation and writing skills. American English.

questions.q: I ___ my keys. Have you seen them?
questions.why: A past action with a result now: present perfect.

questions.q: She ___ here since 2018.
questions.why: 'Since' + present perfect.

questions.q: By the time we arrived, the show ___.
questions.why: The show began BEFORE we arrived: past perfect.

questions.q: I ___ for an hour when he finally arrived.
questions.why: Past perfect continuous: a longer action before another past action.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: How long are you learning English?
How long did you learning English?
How long you have learned English?
How long have you been learning English?
questions.why: 'How long' + present perfect (continuous) for something that started in the past and continues.

questions.q: This is the best pizza I ___.
questions.why: After a superlative we use the present perfect with 'ever'.

questions.q: She ___ the report yet, so she can't send it.
questions.why: 'Yet' with an unfinished action: present perfect.

questions.q: Next June, I ___ in this company for ten years.
questions.why: Future perfect: will have + past participle.

questions.q: He ___ working hard all week, so he is exhausted.
questions.why: Present perfect continuous: has been + -ing.

questions.q: The ground was white. It ___ all night.
questions.why: Past perfect continuous explains the situation in the past.

questions.q: If it rains, we ___ at home.
questions.why: First conditional: if + present, will + base verb.

questions.q: If I were taller, I ___ play basketball.
questions.why: Second conditional: if + past, would + base verb.

questions.q: If she ___ harder, she would have passed.
questions.why: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.q: I wish I ___ more money.
questions.why: 'I wish' + past simple for an unreal present.

questions.q: If I had known, I ___ you.
questions.why: Third conditional result: would have + past participle.

questions.q: Unless you hurry, you ___ the bus.
questions.why: 'Unless' (= if not) with a first conditional.

questions.q: I wish he ___ so loud.
questions.why: 'Wish + would' complains about an annoying habit.

questions.q: If only I ___ the answer yesterday!
questions.why: A regret about the past: 'if only' + past perfect.

questions.q: Had I known about the traffic, I ___ earlier.
questions.why: 'Had I known' means 'If I had known' (third conditional).

questions.q: I'd rather you ___ smoke here.
questions.why: 'Would rather' + a different person uses the past simple.

questions.q: The report ___ by Friday.
questions.why: The report does not finish itself: future passive.

questions.q: Which sentence is passive?
choices: The cake was eaten by my brother.
questions.why: The subject receives the action: was + past participle.

questions.q: This bridge ___ in 1932.
questions.why: Past simple passive: was built.

questions.q: The suspect ___ at the moment.
questions.why: Present continuous passive: is being + past participle.

questions.q: The documents ___ before the meeting.
questions.why: Past perfect passive: had been + past participle.

questions.q: Which sentence is the passive of 'They are repairing the road'?
questions.why: Present continuous passive: is being repaired.

questions.q: I had my car ___ yesterday.
questions.why: 'Have something done' uses the past participle.

questions.q: He is said ___ very rich.
questions.why: 'Is said to be' is a common passive reporting structure.

questions.q: It ___ that the president will resign.
questions.why: 'It is reported that...' is a passive structure.

questions.q: Nobody knows who ___ the window.
questions.why: 'Who' is the subject of an active verb here.

sets.name: Modals of deduction and the past

questions.q: She ___ be at home. The lights are on.
questions.why: 'Must' shows we are almost sure it is true.

questions.q: He ___ be a doctor; he is only ten!
questions.why: 'Can't' shows we are sure it is NOT true.

questions.q: I'm not sure, but they ___ be late.
questions.why: 'Might' shows a possibility.

questions.q: You ___ have called me. I was worried.
questions.why: 'Should have' + past participle criticizes a past action.

questions.q: She ___ have left already. Her bag is gone.
questions.why: 'Must have' + past participle is a deduction about the past.

questions.q: I ___ have gone to the party, but I was ill.
questions.why: 'Could have' shows a past possibility that did not happen.

questions.q: He ___ have done it. He was with me all day.
questions.why: 'Can't have' shows we are sure it did not happen.

questions.q: Look at the wet ground. It ___ rained last night.
questions.why: 'Must have' + past participle: a past deduction.

questions.q: I ___ rather stay home than go out tonight.
questions.why: 'Would rather' shows a preference.

questions.q: You ought ___ told me. It's too late now.
questions.why: 'Ought to have' + past participle shows a past obligation that was ignored.

questions.q: She said, 'I am tired.' She said that she ___ tired.
questions.why: Present simple moves back to past simple.

questions.q: He said, 'I like pizza.' He said he ___ pizza.
questions.why: Reported speech moves the verb one step back.

questions.q: 'I will call you,' she said. She said she ___ me.
questions.why: 'Will' becomes 'would' in reported speech.

questions.q: Following the backshift rule: 'I have finished.' She said she ___.
questions.why: Present perfect becomes past perfect.

questions.q: 'I can swim,' he said. He said he ___ swim.
questions.why: 'Can' becomes 'could'.

questions.q: 'Don't be late,' she told us. She told us ___ late.
questions.why: Negative commands: not + to + base verb.

questions.q: 'Open the window,' he said to me. He asked me ___ the window.
questions.why: Commands become to + base verb.

questions.q: Following the backshift rule: 'I saw her yesterday,' he said. He said he ___ her the day before.
questions.why: Past simple becomes past perfect, and 'yesterday' becomes 'the day before'.

questions.q: 'I'll see you tomorrow,' she said. She said she would see me ___.
questions.why: 'Tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

questions.q: Following the backshift rule: 'Why did you leave?' she asked. She asked me why I ___.
questions.why: In reported questions the tense moves back and the word order is a statement.

questions.q: The man ___ lives next door is a pilot.
questions.why: 'Who' is for people.

questions.q: The movie ___ we watched was boring.
questions.why: 'That' refers to a thing.

questions.q: Is that the girl ___ bag was stolen?
questions.why: 'Whose' shows possession.

questions.q: My uncle, ___ is a chef, cooks well.
questions.why: Extra information between commas: 'who', not 'that'.

questions.q: The reason ___ I called is important.
questions.why: 'The reason why...' is a common phrase.

questions.q: That's the town ___ I grew up.
questions.why: 'Where' refers to a place.

questions.q: The students ___ passed the test were happy.
questions.why: 'Who' is the subject of 'passed'.

questions.q: The woman to ___ I spoke was kind.
questions.why: After a preposition we use 'whom' for people.

questions.q: The book, ___ was published in 1990, is still popular.
questions.why: Extra information between commas uses 'which'.

questions.q: He gave me the answer, ___ surprised everyone.
questions.why: 'Which' can refer to the whole idea in the main clause.

questions.q: I'm interested in ___ photography.
questions.why: After a preposition we use -ing.

questions.q: He promised ___ on time.
questions.why: After 'promise' we use to + base verb.

questions.q: I forgot ___ the milk, so we have none.
questions.why: 'Forget to' = did not do it.

questions.q: I remember ___ this song when I was young.
questions.why: 'Remember + -ing' = a memory of the past.

questions.q: She tried ___ the door, but it was stuck.
questions.why: 'Try to' = make an effort.

questions.q: We stopped ___ some water.
questions.why: 'Stop to' = stop in order to do something.

questions.q: He avoids ___ in public.
questions.why: After 'avoid' we use -ing.

questions.q: It's no use ___ about it.
questions.why: 'It's no use' + -ing.

questions.q: I can't help ___ when I hear that joke.
questions.why: 'Can't help' + -ing.

questions.q: She is not used ___ up early.
questions.why: 'Be used to' + -ing: here 'to' is a preposition.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.why: Put a comma after a greeting, and a question mark at the end.

questions.q: Which sentence is a comma splice?
choices: It was late, we went home.
It was late, so we went home.
It was late. We went home.
It was late; we went home.
questions.why: A comma alone cannot join two complete sentences.

questions.q: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
choices: I love tea; because I am tired.
I love; tea my sister prefers coffee.
I love tea my sister; prefers coffee.
I love tea; my sister prefers coffee.
questions.why: A semicolon joins two related complete sentences.

questions.q: Which sentence uses apostrophes correctly?
choices: The childrens' toys are in the boy's room.
The childrens toys are in the boys room.
The children's toys are in the boys' room.
The children's toy's are in the boys' room.
questions.why: Irregular plural 'children' takes 's; regular plural 'boys' takes only an apostrophe.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: My favorite subjects are, math science and art.
My favorite subjects, are math, science, and art.
My favorite subjects are math, science, and art.
My favorite subjects are math science, and art.
questions.why: Commas separate items in a list.

questions.q: Which phrase uses a hyphen correctly?
questions.why: Join the two words that work together before a noun.

questions.q: Which sentence has parallel structure?
choices: She likes swimming, to run, and cycling.
She likes to swim, running, and cycle.
She likes swimming, running, and cycling.
She likes swim, run, and cycling.
questions.why: Items in a list should have the same form.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.why: Keep the question mark inside the quotation marks, and do not add a comma.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
choices: It's a long way, but the dog knows its way home.
Its a long way, but the dog knows it's way home.
It's a long way, but the dog knows it's way home.
Its a long way, but the dog knows its way home.
questions.why: 'It's' = it is; 'its' shows belonging.

questions.q: Which sentence has NO dangling modifier?
choices: Walking to school, a rainbow appeared.
Walking to school, the rain started.
Walking to school, I saw a rainbow.
Walking to school, the bus was late.
questions.why: The person who is walking must be the subject right after the comma.

questions.q: I need to ___ a decision soon.
questions.why: We say 'make a decision'.

questions.q: Please ___ off your shoes.
questions.why: 'Take off' means to remove clothes.

questions.q: Can you ___ after my cat this weekend?
questions.why: 'Look after' means to take care of.

questions.q: We ran ___ of milk, so I went to the store.
questions.why: 'Run out of' means to have none left.

questions.q: She is afraid ___ spiders.
questions.why: Afraid of + noun.

questions.q: He is responsible ___ the project.
questions.why: Responsible for + noun.

questions.q: I'll ___ you up at 7 a.m.
questions.why: 'Pick up' means to collect someone.

questions.q: The meeting was ___ off because of the storm.
questions.why: 'Call off' means to cancel.

questions.q: She takes ___ her mother.
questions.why: 'Take after' means to look or act like a family member.

questions.q: I can't ___ with this noise any longer.
questions.why: 'Put up with' means to tolerate.

questions.q: ___ it was cold, we went swimming.
questions.why: 'Although' + a clause shows contrast.

questions.q: She was late ___ the traffic.
questions.why: 'Because of' is followed by a noun.

questions.q: He studied hard; ___, he failed.
questions.why: 'However' shows a contrast between two sentences.

questions.q: She is a very ___ student.
questions.why: We need an adjective before 'student'.

questions.q: The ___ between the two cities is 300 km.
questions.why: We need a noun after 'the'.

questions.q: He answered the question ___.
questions.why: We need an adverb to describe 'answered'.

questions.q: ___ the bad weather, the match went ahead.
questions.why: 'In spite of' + a noun shows contrast.

questions.q: I'll lend you the book ___ you give it back.
questions.why: 'As long as' means 'if' (on condition that).

questions.q: She speaks English fluently; ___, she is learning Chinese.
questions.why: 'Furthermore' adds more information.

questions.q: Hardly had she sat down ___ the phone rang.
questions.why: 'Hardly ... when' means 'as soon as'.
